aṣṭāviṃśe tato’ṣṭāṅga-yogena dhyāna-śobhinā |

sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṃ svarūpa-jñānam īryate ||

bhaktiṃ saṅkṣepataḥ procya sāṅkhyām ākhyāya vistṛtam |

entries.literal_english: In the twenty-eighth chapter knowledge of one’s true nature, freed from all limiting adjuncts, is taught through the beautiful meditation of eight-limbed yoga. Having briefly taught devotion and explained Sāṅkhya at length, Hari as Kapila now teaches the Vaiṣṇava eight-limbed yoga. “With seed” means with an object of support; “serene” means having become clear.

entries.sanskrit:
तत्र यम-नियमान् आह त्रिभिर् अक्षर-द्वयाधिकैः । शक्त्या स्व-धर्माचरणम् । ग्राम्यस् त्रैवर्गिको धर्मः, तस्मान् निवृत्तिः । मितं च तन् मेध्यं शुद्धं च तस्यादनम् । तत्र मितं नाम---

> द्वौ भागौ पूरयेद् अन्नैस् तोयेनैकं प्रपूरयेत् । >
> मारुतस्य प्रचारार्थं चतुर्थम् अवशेषयेत् ॥ इति स्मृति-प्रसिद्धम् > ।

विविक्तं विजनं क्षेमं निर्बाधं तस्य स्थानस्य सेवनम् । यावतार्थः प्रयोजनं तावन् मात्रस्य परिग्रहः । आसनादीन्य् अङ्गान्य् आह त्रिभिः । सत आसनस्य जयेन स्थैर्यम् । स्व-धिष्ण्यानां प्राण-स्थानानां मूलाधारादीनां मध्ये एकस्मिन् देशे मनसा सह प्राणस्य धारणं धारणा । आत्मनो मनसः समाधानम् आत्माकारता । अन्यैश् च व्रत-दानादिभिः । पथिभिर् उपायैः ॥२-७॥
word_for_word: there he states the restraints and observances in three [verses], with two additional syllables [in the source’s wording]
performing one’s own duty according to one’s ability
worldly duty directed to the three aims
मितं च तन् मेध्यं शुद्धं च तस्यादनम्
and moderate, fit, pure food is to be eaten
द्वौ भागौ पूरयेद् अन्नैस् तोयेनैकं प्रपूरयेत्
fill two parts with food and one part with water
leave the fourth part for the movement of air
विविक्तं विजनं क्षेमं निर्बाधं तस्य स्थानस्य सेवनम्
use a secluded, solitary, safe, undisturbed place
acquire only as much as is needed for the purpose
he states the limbs beginning with posture in three [verses]
steadiness comes from mastery of posture
स्व-धिष्ण्यानां प्राण-स्थानानां मूलाधारादीनां मध्ये एकस्मिन् देशे
in one place among the seats of the breath, such as the mūlādhāra
holding the breath together with the mind is dhāraṇā
settling the mind as the Self
and by other means such as vows and gifts
entries.literal_english: There he states the yamas and niyamas in three [verses], with “two additional syllables” in the source’s compressed wording. Performing one’s own duty according to one’s ability is [a rule]. Worldly duty directed to the three aims is to be left behind. One should eat moderate, clean and pure food. “Moderate” is defined in a well-known Smṛti: fill two parts with food, one part with water, and leave the fourth empty for the movement of air. One should stay in a secluded, solitary, safe and undisturbed place; one should acquire only as much as is needed. He states the limbs beginning with posture in three [verses]. Steadiness comes from mastering one’s posture. Holding the breath with the mind in one place among the breath’s seats, such as the mūlādhāra, is dhāraṇā. Settling the mind as the Self is [samādhi]. Other means include vows and gifts.

entries.sanskrit:
आसनादीनि प्रपञ्चयति---शुचाव् इति यावत् समाप्ति । आसनं कुशाजिन-चैलोत्तरं प्रतिष्ठाप्य । स्वस्तिकासनेन यथा-सुखम् इति वा । समभ्यसेत् प्राणम् इति शेषः ।

> ऊरू जङ्घान्तर् आधाय पादाग्रे जानु-मध्यगे । >
> योगिनो यद् अवस्थानं स्वस्तिकं तद् विदुर् बुधाः ॥ इति ॥८॥
word_for_word: he expands upon posture and the other limbs
with cloth over antelope skin and kuśa grass

transliteration:
āsanādīni prapañcayati---śucāv iti yāvat samāpti | āsanaṃ kuśājina-cailottaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya | svastikāsanena yathā-sukham iti vā | samabhyaset prāṇam iti śeṣaḥ |

> ūrū jaṅghāntar ādhāya pādāgre jānu-madhyage | >
> yogino yad avasthānaṃ svastikaṃ tad vidur budhāḥ || iti ||8||
entries.literal_english: He expands on posture and the other limbs beginning with “in a clean place.” One should establish a seat with cloth over antelope skin and kuśa grass, and sit comfortably, for example in svastikāsana; the understood continuation is that one should then practise regulation of the breath. The cited verse defines svastikāsana by placing the feet between the thighs and calves with the tips near the knees.

entries.sanskrit: बाह्य-वायोर् अन्तः प्रवेशनं पूरकः, प्रवेशितस्य धारणं कुम्भकः, धृतस्य बहिर् निःसारणं रेचकः । प्रतिकूलेन वा रेचक-कुम्भक-पूरकैः । यद् वा, इडया पूर्य पिङ्गलया रेचनम्, पिङ्गलया पूर्य इडया रेचनम् इत्य् एवं प्रतिकूलेन । वा-शब्दश् चार्थे । स्थिरं सत् पुनर् अपि चञ्चलं यथा न भवति तथा शोधयेत् ॥९॥
word_for_word: the outer breath’s entering within is pūraka
retaining what has entered is kumbhaka
letting out what has been retained is recaka
or in reverse order through recaka, kumbhaka and pūraka
inhaling through iḍā and exhaling through piṅgalā
inhaling through piṅgalā and exhaling through iḍā
स्थिरं सत् पुनर् अपि चञ्चलं यथा न भवति तथा शोधयेत्
one should purify it so that, once steady, it does not become restless again
entries.literal_english: The inward movement of the outer breath is pūraka; retaining it after it has entered is kumbhaka; letting out what has been retained is recaka. Or the order may be reversed through recaka, kumbhaka and pūraka. Alternatively, one may inhale through iḍā and exhale through piṅgalā, then inhale through piṅgalā and exhale through iḍā. “Or” indicates another option. One should purify the breath so that, once steady, it does not become restless again.

entries.sanskrit: ध्मातं सन्तप्तम् इत्य् अर्थः । लोहं सुवर्णं यथा मलं त्यजति तथा मनो विरजं स्यात् । ततश् चञ्चलं न स्याद् इति भावः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: just as gold metal gives up its dross
so the mind should become stainless
ततश् चञ्चलं न स्याद् इति भावः
then it will not be restless; this is the meaning
entries.literal_english: “Dhmātam” means heated. Just as gold metal gives up its dross when heated, the mind should become free of impurity; then it will no longer be restless.

entries.sanskrit: प्राणायाम् आदीनां समाधौ द्वारकार्याण्य् आह---प्राणायामैर् इति । दोषान् वात-श्लेष्मादीन् । संसर्गान् विषय-संसर्गान् । अनीश्वरान् रागादीन् । वायुना सह मनसः स्थिरी-करणं धारणा, स्थिरस्य वृत्ति-सन्ततिः ध्यानम्, वृत्ति-निरोधः समाधिर् इति भेदः ॥११॥
word_for_word: he explains how prāṇāyāma and the other practices serve as gateways to samādhi
the faults: wind, phlegm and the like
uncontrolled forces: attachment and the like
steadying the mind together with the breath is dhāraṇā
the uninterrupted flow of the steady mental state is dhyāna
the stopping of mental activity is samādhi
entries.literal_english: He explains how prāṇāyāma and the other practices serve as gateways to samādhi. The “faults” are wind and phlegm and the like; “associations” are contacts with sense objects; the uncontrolled forces are attachment and the like. Steadying the mind together with the breath is dhāraṇā; the uninterrupted flow of a steady mental state is dhyāna; stopping mental activity is samādhi.

entries.sanskrit: सुसमाहितं स्थिरं जातम् । काष्ठां कलाम् । मूर्तिम् इत्य् अर्थः । स्व-नासाग्रेऽवलोकनं यस्य । एतच् च लय-विक्षेपयोः परिहाराय ॥१२॥

entries.literal_english: “Well concentrated” means made steady. Kāṣṭhā means a form or definite manifestation. His gaze is directed toward the tip of his own nose. This is prescribed to prevent both mental sinking and distraction.

entries.sanskrit: ध्येयं हरिम् आह सप्तभिः । प्रसन्नं वदनाम्भोजं यस्य तं ध्ययेद् इति षष्ठेनान्वयः । पद्म-गर्भ-वद् अरुणे ईक्षणे नेत्रे यस्य । नीलोत्पल-दल-वच् छ्यामम् ॥१३॥
word_for_word: Hari as the object of meditation
eyes reddish like the interior of a lotus

entries.literal_english: In seven verses he describes Hari as the object of meditation. The construction is: one should meditate upon Him whose lotus face is serene. His eyes are reddish like the interior of a lotus, and His complexion is dark like a blue-lotus petal.

entries.sanskrit: लसत्-पङ्कजस्य किञ्जल्कवत्पीते कौशेये वाससी यस्य । श्रीवत्सो लाञ्छनं वक्षसि यस्य । भ्राजत् कौस्तुभेनामुक्ता संश्लिष्टा कन्धरा यस्य ।

whose chest bears the Śrīvatsa mark
भ्राजत् कौस्तुभेन आमुक्ता संश्लिष्टा कन्धरा यस्य

entries.literal_english: His silken garments are yellow like the filaments of a shining lotus. The Śrīvatsa mark is on his chest. His neck is adorned with the shining Kaustubha jewel.

entries.sanskrit: मत्त-द्विरेफाणां कलो मधुरो ध्वनिर् यस्यां तया । परीतं व्याप्तम् । परार्ध्यान्य् अमूल्यानि हारादीनि यस्य ॥१५॥

entries.literal_english: The garland is filled with the soft, sweet sound of intoxicated bees. “Parīta” means filled or pervaded. He wears necklaces and other ornaments of priceless value.

entries.sanskrit: काञ्ची-गुणेनोल्लसन्ती श्रोणी यस्य । भक्तानां हृदयाम्भोजम् एव विष्टरम् आसनं यस्य । भक्तानां मनो-नयनानि वर्धयति हर्षयतीति तथा ॥१६॥

entries.sanskrit: अपीच्यम् अति-सुन्दरं भक्त-विषयं दर्शनं यस्य । कैशोरे तारुण्ये वयसि सन्तं स्थितम् । भृत्यानाम् अनुग्रहे कातरं व्यग्रम् ॥१७॥

situated in the youthful age of adolescence
eager; intent on showing favor to his attendants
entries.literal_english: His vision is exceedingly beautiful and an object of the devotees’ love. He remains in the youthful age of adolescence, and is eager to show favor to his attendants.

entries.literal_english: His fame is tīrtha—purifying and worthy of praise—and it bestows fame upon holy persons such as Bali. All limbs are complete in Him. “Does not depart” means that the mind neither slips away nor wanders elsewhere.

entries.sanskrit: प्रेक्षणीयम् ईहितं लीला यस्य ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: His playful activities are a delight to behold.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं समग्र-ध्यानम् उक्त्वैकैकावयव-ध्यानम् आह---**तस्मिन्** **लब्धं पदं** स्थितिर् येन तच् **चित्तं** **विलक्ष्य**, विशेषेण लक्षी-कृत्य । **एकत्र** एकैकस्मिन्न् अङ्ग इत्य् अर्थः ॥२०॥
word_for_word: upon one limb at a time

entries.literal_english: Having thus taught meditation on the complete form, he teaches meditation on each individual limb. One should mark the mind that has attained a settled position in Him and focus it especially; “in one place” means upon one limb at a time.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एव पादादि-क्रमेणाह त्रयोदशभिः । **सम्यक् चिन्तयेत्** । पाद-तले रेखात्मकानि वज्रादीनि **लाञ्छनानि**, तैः **आढ्यं** युक्तम् । उत्तुङ्गाश् च रक्ताश् च विलसन्तो नखास् तेषां चक्रवालं मण्डलं तस्य ज्योत्स्नाभिर् आहतो **महतां** ध्यातॄणां **हृदयान्ध-कारो** येन । एतच् च सर्वम् उपादेय-विशेषणं ध्येयत्वेनैवोच्यते ॥२१॥
word_for_word: in order beginning with the feet

transliteration: tad eva pādādi-krameṇāha trayodaśabhiḥ | **samyak cintayet** | pāda-tale rekhātmakāni vajrādīni **lāñchanāni**, taiḥ **āḍhyaṃ** yuktam | uttuṅgāś ca raktāś ca vilasanto nakhās teṣāṃ cakravālaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tasya jyotsnābhir āhato **mahatāṃ** dhyātṝṇāṃ **hṛdayāndha-kāro** yena | etac ca sarvam upādeya-viśeṣaṇaṃ dhyeyatvenaivocyate ||21||
entries.literal_english: He now describes this in thirteen verses, beginning with the feet. One should contemplate well the Lord’s soles, rich with line-shaped marks such as the thunderbolt. The circle of His high, reddish, shining nails sends out moonlight-like rays that strike away the darkness in the hearts of great meditators. All these qualifying features are stated precisely as objects of meditation.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, यस्य **शौचेन** क्षालनेन **निःसृतायाः** **सरित्-प्रवराया** गङ्गाया **उदकेन** **तीर्थेन** संसार-तारकेण **मूर्ध्न्य् अधिकृतेन** धृतेन **शिवोऽपि शिवोऽभूत्**, अत्यधिकं सुखं प्रापेत्य् अर्थः । ध्यातुर् **मनसि यः शमल-शैलः** पाप-पर्वतस् तस्मिन् **निसृष्टं** क्सिप्तं **वज्रम्** इव यत् । यद् वा, शमल-शैले निसृष्टं स्व-लाञ्छन-रूपं वज्रं येन तत् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: यस्य शौचेन क्षालनेन निःसृतायाः सरित्-प्रवराया गङ्गायाः
of the Ganges, the foremost river, which flowed from washing his feet
by its water, a sacred ford that carries one across saṃsāra
when held upon his head, even Śiva became auspicious
he attained supreme happiness; this is the meaning
the mountain of sin in the meditator’s mind
तस्मिन् निसृष्टं क्षिप्तं वज्रम् इव यत्
that which is like a thunderbolt hurled at it
यद् वा शमल-शैले निसृष्टं स्व-लाञ्छन-रूपं वज्रं येन तत्
or, he who hurls his own emblem, the thunderbolt, at the mountain of sin
entries.literal_english: Moreover, the water of the Ganges—the foremost river that flowed from the washing of his feet—is a sacred ford that carries beings across saṃsāra. When Śiva held it upon his head, even he became auspicious and attained supreme happiness. For the meditator, that water is like a thunderbolt hurled at the mountain of sin in the mind. Alternatively, the verse describes the Lord’s foot as his own emblem, a thunderbolt hurled at that mountain of sin.

entries.sanskrit: विभोर्** **जानु-द्वयं** तत्-पर्यन्तं जङ्घा-द्वयम् **अखिलस्य** **विधातुर्** ब्रह्मणो **जनन्या** **लक्ष्म्या** **संलालितं** स्पर्श-चातुर्येण संसेवितम् । संसारित्वम् इव प्रतीतं वारयति---**अभवस्य** इति । **हृदि कुर्याद्** ध्यायेत् ॥२३॥
word_for_word: one should place in the heart, meditate

transliteration: vibhor** **jānu-dvayaṃ** tat-paryantaṃ jaṅghā-dvayam **akhilasya** **vidhātur** brahmaṇo **jananyā** **lakṣmyā** **saṃlālitaṃ** sparśa-cāturyeṇa saṃsevitam | saṃsāritvam iva pratītaṃ vārayati---**abhavasya** iti | **hṛdi kuryād** dhyāyet ||23||
entries.literal_english: One should place in the heart—that is, meditate upon—the Lord’s two knees and the two shanks extending to them, lovingly served with expert touch by Lakṣmī, mother of Brahmā, the creator of all. The word “unborn” prevents the mistaken impression that the Lord is subject to saṃsāra.

entries.sanskrit: सुपर्णस्य भुजयोः** स्कन्धयोर् **अधि** उपरि । **ओजसो** बलस्य **निधी** आधारौ । **अतसिकायाः कुसुमवत्** कान्त्या **अवभासमानौ** । **व्यालम्बि** आगुल्फं लम्बमानं यत् **पीताम्बरं वासस्** तस्मिन् **वर्तमानो** यः **काञ्ची-कलापस्** तेन **परिरम्भः** संश्लेषो विद्यते यस्य तद् विभोर् **नितम्ब-बिम्बं** च हृदि कुर्याद् इति पूर्वेणैवान्वयः ॥२४॥
word_for_word: above the shoulders on Suparṇa’s arms
shining with the color of the flax flower
व्यालम्बि आगुल्फं लम्बमानं यत् पीताम्बरं वासस् तस्मिन् वर्तमानो यः काञ्ची-कलापस्
the girdle that lies over the yellow garment hanging down to the ankles
तद् विभोर् नितम्ब-बिम्बं च हृदि कुर्याद्
one should also hold the Lord’s rounded hips in the heart
thus it is construed with the preceding passage
entries.literal_english: “Above the arms of Suparṇa” means above Garuḍa’s shoulders. The Lord’s thighs are supports of strength and shine with the color of the flax flower. He wears a girdle wrapped around him over the yellow garment that hangs down to his ankles. The Lord’s rounded hips should also be held in the heart, continuing the construction of the previous verse.

entries.sanskrit: अमुष्य** हरेर् **नाभि-ह्रदं** ध्यायेत् । कथं-भूतम् ? **भुवनानां कोशस्य** समूहस्य **गुहा** अधिष्ठानं यद् **उदरं** तत्र **स्थितम्** । **यत्र** नाभि-ह्रदे **आत्म-योनेर्** ब्रह्मणो **धिषणं** धिष्ण्यम् **अखिल-लोकात्मकं पद्मं** **व्यूढम्** उत्थितम् । तथा **हरिन्-मणि-वृषौ** मरकत-मणि-श्रेष्ठाव् इव यौ **स्तनौ**, तयोर् **द्वयं ध्यायेत्**। **विशद-हाराणां मयूखैर् गौरं** श्वेतम् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: hidden support of the aggregate of worlds

transliteration: amuṣya** harer **nābhi-hradaṃ** dhyāyet | kathaṃ-bhūtam ? **bhuvanānāṃ kośasya** samūhasya **guhā** adhiṣṭhānaṃ yad **udaraṃ** tatra **sthitam** | **yatra** nābhi-hrade **ātma-yoner** brahmaṇo **dhiṣaṇaṃ** dhiṣṇyam **akhila-lokātmakaṃ padmaṃ** **vyūḍham** utthitam | tathā **harin-maṇi-vṛṣau** marakata-maṇi-śreṣṭhāv iva yau **stanau**, tayor **dvayaṃ dhyāyet**| **viśada-hārāṇāṃ mayūkhair gauraṃ** śvetam ||25||
entries.literal_english: One should meditate on Hari’s lake-like navel, situated in the abdomen that is the hidden support of the aggregate of worlds. From that navel arose the lotus that is the seat of self-born Brahmā and embodies all worlds. One should also meditate on His two breasts, like the finest emeralds, made fair by the rays of His spotless necklaces.

entries.sanskrit: ऋषभस्य** श्रेष्ठस्य **महा-विभूतेर्** महा-लक्ष्म्या **अधिवासं** स्थानं **वक्षः** **कण्ठं च मनसि कुर्यात्** । कथं-भूतं कण्ठम् ? **कौस्तुभ-मणिर्** यो **भूषणार्थं** धृतः, तस्य **अधिकं** भूषणम् अर्थः प्रयोजनं यस्य । कौस्तुभ-मणिम् एव स्वयम् अलङ्कुर्वन्तम् इत्य् अर्थः । **पुंसां** स्मर्तॄणां च **मनो-नयनानां निर्वृतिम् आदधानम्** इत्य् उभयोर् विशेषणम् ॥२६॥

transliteration: ṛṣabhasya** śreṣṭhasya **mahā-vibhūter** mahā-lakṣmyā **adhivāsaṃ** sthānaṃ **vakṣaḥ** **kaṇṭhaṃ ca manasi kuryāt** | kathaṃ-bhūtaṃ kaṇṭham ? **kaustubha-maṇir** yo **bhūṣaṇārthaṃ** dhṛtaḥ, tasya **adhikaṃ** bhūṣaṇam arthaḥ prayojanaṃ yasya | kaustubha-maṇim eva svayam alaṅkurvantam ity arthaḥ | **puṃsāṃ** smartṝṇāṃ ca **mano-nayanānāṃ nirvṛtim ādadhānam** ity ubhayor viśeṣaṇam ||26||
entries.literal_english: One should contemplate the chest and neck of the Supreme Lord, the abode of Mahā-Lakṣmī. His neck is such an ornament that it ornaments the Kaustubha jewel itself, though that jewel is worn as an ornament. Both chest and neck bring delight to the minds and eyes of those who remember Him.

entries.sanskrit: निर्णिक्तान्य्** उज्ज्वली-कृतानि **बाहु-वलयान्य्** अङ्गदानि येषु । **अधि** श्रिता **लोक-पाला** येषु । **दश-शतारं** चक्रम् । **न सह्यं तेजो** यस्य । कर-सरोरुहे राज-हंसम् इव ॥२७॥
word_for_word: like a royal swan on the lotus hand
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nirṇiktāny** ujjvalī-kṛtāni **bāhu-valayāny** aṅgadāni yeṣu | **adhi** śritā **loka-pālā** yeṣu | **daśa-śatāraṃ** cakram | **na sahyaṃ tejo** yasya | kara-saroruhe rāja-haṃsam iva ||27||
entries.literal_english: His armlets and bracelets are polished and made radiant; the guardians of the worlds take refuge in His arms. His discus has a thousand spokes and unbearable brilliance, and rests upon His lotus hand like a royal swan.

entries.sanskrit:
अरातयो** ये **भटा** योद्धारः, तेषां **शोणितम्** एव **कर्दमः,** तेन **दिग्धां** लिप्ताम् । **अस्य कण्ठे मालां मणिं** च **स्मरेत्** । **मधुव्रताणां वरूथस्य गिरा उपघुष्टां** नादिताम् । चैत्त्यस्य जीवस्य तत्त्वम् । तद् उक्तं वैष्णवे---

> आत्मानम् अस्य जगतो निर्लेपम् अगुणामलम् । >
> बिभर्ति कौस्तुभ-मणि-स्वरूपं भगवान् हरिः ॥ \[वि।पु। > १.२२.६८\] इति ॥२८ ॥
word_for_word: one should remember the garland and jewel
with the humming of a swarm of bees
the principle of the individual living being
in the form of the Kaustubha jewel

transliteration:
arātayo** ye **bhaṭā** yoddhāraḥ, teṣāṃ **śoṇitam** eva **kardamaḥ,** tena **digdhāṃ** liptām | **asya kaṇṭhe mālāṃ maṇiṃ** ca **smaret** | **madhuvratāṇāṃ varūthasya girā upaghuṣṭāṃ** nāditām | caittyasya jīvasya tattvam | tad uktaṃ vaiṣṇave---

> ātmānam asya jagato nirlepam aguṇāmalam | >
> bibharti kaustubha-maṇi-svarūpaṃ bhagavān hariḥ || \[vi|pu| > 1.22.68\] iti ||28 ||
entries.literal_english: One should remember His garland, smeared with the blood of enemy warriors as though with mud, and the jewel at His neck. The garland resounds with the humming of swarms of bees. The Kaustubha represents the principle of the individual living being; hence the cited Viṣṇu Purāṇa says that Hari bears the stainless, quality-transcending Self of the universe in the form of the Kaustubha jewel.

entries.sanskrit: भृत्येष्व् अनुकम्पिता कृतानुकम्पा या धीस् तया गृहीता मूर्तिर् येन तस्य । विस्फुरती ये मकर-कुण्डले तयोर् वल्गितेन प्रचलनेन विद्योतिताव् अमलौ कपोलौ यस्मिंस् तत् । उदारा उन्नता नासा यस्मिंस् तत् ॥२९॥

transliteration: bhṛtyeṣv anukampitā kṛtānukampā yā dhīs tayā gṛhītā mūrtir yena tasya | visphuratī ye makara-kuṇḍale tayor valgitena pracalanena vidyotitāv amalau kapolau yasmiṃs tat | udārā unnatā nāsā yasmiṃs tat ||29||
entries.literal_english: The Lord assumes His form through a compassionate intention toward His servants. His spotless cheeks are illumined by the swinging of His flashing makara-shaped earrings, and His nose is noble and prominent.

entries.sanskrit: यच् च स्वय भूत्या शोभयालिभिः परिसेव्यमानं मीन-द्वयाश्रयं च श्री-निकेतनं पद्मम् अधिक्षिपद् वर्तते तद् ध्यायेत् । तत्र कुन्तलैर् अलीनाम् अधिक्सेपः । नेत्र-द्वयेन मीन-द्वयस्येति द्रष्टव्यम् । अब्जे इव नेत्रे यस्मिन्न् इत्य् उपमानान्तरम् । उल्लसन्त्यौ भ्रुवौ यस्मिन् । मनो-मयं मनस्य् अविर्भवत् ॥३०॥
word_for_word: surpassing the lotus, abode of Śrī
the two eyes surpass the pair of fish

transliteration: yac ca svaya bhūtyā śobhayālibhiḥ parisevyamānaṃ mīna-dvayāśrayaṃ ca śrī-niketanaṃ padmam adhikṣipad vartate tad dhyāyet | tatra kuntalair alīnām adhiksepaḥ | netra-dvayena mīna-dvayasyeti draṣṭavyam | abje iva netre yasminn ity upamānāntaram | ullasantyau bhruvau yasmin | mano-mayaṃ manasy avirbhavat ||30||
entries.literal_english: One should meditate on the face that by its own beauty surpasses a lotus—the abode of Śrī, attended by bees and sheltering a pair of fish. The curls surpass the bees and the two eyes surpass the pair of fish; alternatively, His eyes are themselves like lotuses. His brows shine, and the form manifests within the mind.

entries.sanskrit: कृपयाधिकम् अत्यर्थम् । अक्षिभ्यां निसृष्टं प्रयुक्तम् । स्निग्ध-स्मितेनानुगुणितं संयुक्तम् । विपुलः प्रसादो यस्मिन् । गुहायां हृदि ॥३१॥

entries.sanskrit: अवनता येऽखिल-लोकास् तेषां तीव्र-शोकेन यान्य् अश्रूणि तेषां सागरं विशोषयतीति तथा तं हरेर् हासम् । अस्यात्य्-उदारं भ्रू-मण्डलं च ध्यायेत् । कथं भूतम् । निज-मायया मकर-ध्वजस्यापि संमोहनाय रचितम् । मुनि-कृते मुनीनाम् उपकाराय । मुनीनां संमोहने प्रवृत्तं कामम् एव संमोहयितुम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥

entries.literal_english: One should meditate on Hari’s smile, which dries up the ocean of tears produced by the intense sorrow of all the bowed worlds, and on His exceedingly noble brows. By His own māyā those brows are fashioned to bewilder even Cupid; for the benefit of the sages, they bewilder Cupid himself when he sets out to bewilder the sages.

entries.sanskrit: मन्द-हास-ध्यानम् उक्त्वा स्फुट-हास-ध्यानम् आह---विष्णोः **प्रहसितम्** उच्चैर् हसितं **ध्यायेत्** । कीदृशम् ? **ध्यानायनम्** अतिसुन्दरतया प्रयत्नं विनैव ध्यानस्य विषय-भूतम् । सौन्दर्यम् एवाह---**बहुलया** अधिकया **अधरोष्ठस्य** **भासा** कान्त्या **आरुणी-भूतास् तनवः** सूक्ष्मा **द्विजा** एव **कुन्द**-मुकुलानि, तेषां **पङ्क्तिः** स्फुरति यस्मिंस् तत् । **देह-कुहरे** हृदयाकाशेऽ**वसितस्य** ज्ञातस्य । प्रेम-रसेन **आर्द्रया भक्त्या** तस्मिन्न् एव **अर्पित-मनाः** सन् **पृथक्** तद्-व्यतिरिक्तं **द्रष्टुं नेच्छेत्** । न चित्तं विचालयेद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३३॥

entries.literal_english: After teaching meditation on the gentle smile, he teaches meditation on Viṣṇu’s open laughter. It is naturally an object of meditation because of its extraordinary beauty. The abundant radiance of His lower lip makes the fine teeth, like rows of jasmine buds, appear reddish. Having known Him within the cavity of the body, the heart-space, the devotee whose mind is offered to Him alone through devotion moistened by the nectar of love should not wish to see anything separate from Him; that is, the mind should not be moved elsewhere.

समाधिम् आह---एवम् इति द्वाभ्याम् । निर्बीजः सबीजश् चेति द्वि-विधो योगः । तत्र निर्बीज-योगे---

> यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश् चञ्चलम् अस्थिरम् । >
> ततस् ततो नियम्यैतद् आत्मन्य् एव वशं नयेत् ॥ \[गीता ६.२६\]

इति गीताद्य्-उक्त-मार्गेण क्रियमाणोऽपि दुष्करः समाधिः । स-बीजे तु सुकरः । तत्र हि परमानन्द-मूर्तौ हरौ ध्यायमानेऽयत्नत एव चित्तोपरमो भवति । तद् उक्तम्---हृतात्मनो हृत-प्राणांश् च भक्तिर् अनिच्छतो मे गतिम् अण्वीं प्रयुङ्क्ते \[भा।पु। ३.२५.३६\] इति। अतः स एवोपक्षिप्तो योगस्य लक्षणं वक्ष्ये स-बीजस्येति । तद् एवायत्न-सिद्धत्वं दर्शयति---एवं ध्यान-मार्गेण **हरौ प्रतिलब्धो भावः** प्रेमा येन, तथा **भक्त्या द्रवद्-धृदयं** यस्य, **प्रमोदाद् उद्गतानि पुलकानि** यस्य । **औत्कण्ठ्य**-प्रवृत्त्**आश्रु-कलया** च **मुहुर् अर्द्यमान** आनन्द-संप्लवे निमज्जमानो दुर्ग्रहस्य भगवतो ग्रहणे **बडिशं** मत्स्य-वेधनम् इवोपाय-भूतं **चित्तम्** अपि ध्येयाद् **वियुङ्क्ते** । तद्-धारणे शिथिल-प्रयत्नो भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३४॥

iti gītādy-ukta-mārgeṇa kriyamāṇo’pi duṣkaraḥ samādhiḥ | sa-bīje tu sukaraḥ | tatra hi paramānanda-mūrtau harau dhyāyamāne’yatnata eva cittoparamo bhavati | tad uktam---hṛtātmano hṛta-prāṇāṃś ca bhaktir anicchato me gatim aṇvīṃ prayuṅkte \[bhā|pu| 3.25.36\] iti| ataḥ sa evopakṣipto yogasya lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye sa-bījasyeti | tad evāyatna-siddhatvaṃ darśayati---evaṃ dhyāna-mārgeṇa **harau pratilabdho bhāvaḥ** premā yena, tathā **bhaktyā dravad-dhṛdayaṃ** yasya, **pramodād udgatāni pulakāni** yasya | **autkaṇṭhya**-pravṛtt**āśru-kalayā** ca **muhur ardyamāna** ānanda-saṃplave nimajjamāno durgrahasya bhagavato grahaṇe **baḍiśaṃ** matsya-vedhanam ivopāya-bhūtaṃ **cittam** api dhyeyād **viyuṅkte** | tad-dhāraṇe śithila-prayatno bhavatīty arthaḥ ||34||
entries.literal_english: In two verses he describes samādhi. Yoga is of two kinds, seedless and with seed. Seedless samādhi, practised by repeatedly restraining the wandering mind as taught in the Gītā, is difficult; meditation with seed is easy, because when Hari, the embodiment of supreme bliss, is meditated upon, the mind naturally comes to rest. Thus the yogin whose love for Hari has arisen through meditation, whose heart melts through devotion, whose hairs stand on end from joy, and who is repeatedly drenched by tears of longing and submerged in a flood of bliss, eventually loosens even the mind—the hook by which the otherwise hard-to-grasp Lord was grasped—from the object of meditation.

entries.sanskrit: यर्हि** यदैवं **निर्विषयं** भगवति, अत एव **मुक्ताश्रयं** च । ध्येय-सम्बन्धं विना ध्यातर्य् अवस्थानासम्भवात् । न च पूर्ववच् छब्दादिर् विषयः स्यात् । यतस् तत्र **विरक्तं** परमानन्दानुभवेन । अतो **निर्वाणं** लयम् **ऋच्छति** । वृत्ति-रूपतां परित्यज्य ब्रह्माकारेण परिणमत इत्य् अर्थः, **यथा अर्चिर्** ज्वालाश्रय-विषयापगमे महा-भूत-ज्योती-रूपेण परिणमते । **अत्र** अस्यां दशायाम् **अव्यवधानं** ध्यातृ-ध्येय-विभाग-शून्यम् **एकम्** अखण्डम् **आत्मानम्** **अनु**गतम् **ईक्षते** । अत्र हेतुः---**प्रतिनिवृत्तो**ऽपगतो **गुण-प्रवाहो** देहाद्य्-उपाधिर् यस्य ॥३५॥

transliteration: yarhi** yadaivaṃ **nirviṣayaṃ** bhagavati, ata eva **muktāśrayaṃ** ca | dhyeya-sambandhaṃ vinā dhyātary avasthānāsambhavāt | na ca pūrvavac chabdādir viṣayaḥ syāt | yatas tatra **viraktaṃ** paramānandānubhavena | ato **nirvāṇaṃ** layam **ṛcchati** | vṛtti-rūpatāṃ parityajya brahmākāreṇa pariṇamata ity arthaḥ, **yathā arcir** jvālāśraya-viṣayāpagame mahā-bhūta-jyotī-rūpeṇa pariṇamate | **atra** asyāṃ daśāyām **avyavadhānaṃ** dhyātṛ-dhyeya-vibhāga-śūnyam **ekam** akhaṇḍam **ātmānam** **anu**gatam **īkṣate** | atra hetuḥ---**pratinivṛtto**’pagato **guṇa-pravāho** dehādy-upādhir yasya ||35||
entries.literal_english: When the mind is thus without external object and has the Lord alone as its support, it cannot remain as a meditator apart from the object meditated upon. Having become detached from sound and other objects through the experience of supreme bliss, it reaches dissolution: abandoning the form of a mental modification, it assumes the form of Brahman, just as a flame, when separated from its fuel, resolves into the element fire. In this state one sees the single, undivided Self without the division of meditator and meditated object, because the flow of the guṇas—the bodily and other limiting adjuncts—has withdrawn.

entries.sanskrit:
न च सुप्तोत्थित इव पुनः संसरतीत्य् आह---सोऽपि स एव पुरुषस् तस्मिन् महिम्नि ब्रह्म-रूपेऽवसितोऽवसानं निष्ठां प्राप्तः । कया ? मनसो निवृत्त्या चरमयाऽविद्या-रहितयेति सुषुप्ताद् विशेषः । तत्र ह्य् अविद्यास्ति, न त्व् इदानीम् । अत्र हेतुः, एतया योगाभ्यास-कृतयेत्य् अर्थः ।

नन्व् एवम् अपि **सुख-दुःखयोर्** आत्म-धर्मत्वे कुतो ब्रह्मैक्यं ? तत्राह---दुःखयोः सुख-दुःखयोर् **हेतुत्वं** भोक्तृत्वं च यत् पूर्वम् आसीत्, तद् अप्य् **असत्य्** अविद्या-कृते **कर्तर्य्** अहङ्कारे **विधत्ते** । तन्-निष्ठम् एव पश्यतीत्य् अर्थः । यत **उपलब्ध-परात्म-काष्ठो**ऽपरोक्षी-कृतात्म-तत्त्वः ॥३६॥

entries.literal_english: He says that the liberated person does not return to saṃsāra as one who has merely awakened from sleep. That same person has reached the final state in the glory of Brahman. How? Through the final withdrawal of the mind, which is free from ignorance; this distinguishes it from deep sleep, where ignorance remains. The cause is this state produced by the practice of yoga. One may object: if pleasure and pain belong to the Self, how can there be unity with Brahman? He answers: the former sense of being an agent and experiencer of pleasure and pain was itself unreal, imposed by ignorance upon the ego. The person sees that it rested only there. He has directly realized the supreme limit of the Self.

entries.sanskrit: स्वरूपं जीव-ब्रह्मणोर् याथार्थ्यम् अध्यगमत् । तस्य जीवन्-मुक्तिम् आह---देहं चेति द्वाभ्याम्---चरम उक्त-लक्षणः सिद्धो देहम् अपि न विपश्यति, कुतः सुख-दुःखे ? आसनाद् उत्थितम् उत्थाय तत्रैव स्थितं तत्-स्थानाद् अपेतं ततो दैव-वशात् पुनर् अप्य् उपेतं वा न विपश्यति । यतः स्वरूपं प्राप्तः । यतो देहात् स्वरूपम् अध्यगमत् तं देहम् इति वा । सतोऽप्य् अननुसन्धाने दृष्टान्तः, वासः परिकृतं कटि-तटे परिवेष्टितं स्थितं गतं वा मदिरा-मदेनान्धो यथा न पश्यति ॥३७॥

transliteration: svarūpaṃ jīva-brahmaṇor yāthārthyam adhyagamat | tasya jīvan-muktim āha---dehaṃ ceti dvābhyām---carama ukta-lakṣaṇaḥ siddho deham api na vipaśyati, kutaḥ sukha-duḥkhe ? āsanād utthitam utthāya tatraiva sthitaṃ tat-sthānād apetaṃ tato daiva-vaśāt punar apy upetaṃ vā na vipaśyati | yataḥ svarūpaṃ prāptaḥ | yato dehāt svarūpam adhyagamat taṃ deham iti vā | sato’py ananusandhāne dṛṣṭāntaḥ, vāsaḥ parikṛtaṃ kaṭi-taṭe pariveṣṭitaṃ sthitaṃ gataṃ vā madirā-madenāndho yathā na paśyati ||37||
entries.literal_english: He has realized the true nature of the individual self and Brahman. Śrīdhara now describes liberation while living: the accomplished yogin of the stated kind does not even notice the body, much less its pleasure and pain—whether it has risen from its seat, remains there, leaves that place, or by destiny returns to it—because he has attained his true nature. As an analogy for failure to notice something still present, a person blinded by intoxication does not notice whether the garment wrapped around his waist remains or has fallen away.

entries.sanskrit: एवं प्रतिबुद्ध-वस्तुर् इति । देहोऽ**पि** इत्य् आदौ चेति । तस्माद् अस्य प्रारब्ध-कर्म-मात्राणाम् अनभिनिवेशेनैव भोगः । एवम् एवोक्तं---तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वम् अनुपश्यतः\[ईशोपनिषद् ७\] इति । ननु तर्हि देहस्य कथं प्रवृत्ति-निवृत्ती जीवनं वा ? तत्राह---देहोऽपीति । दैवं पूर्व-संस्कारः, तद्-वशेन गच्छन् यावत् स्वारम्भकं कर्मास्ति तावत् प्रतिसमीक्षते जीवत्य् एव । सासुः सेन्द्रियः । ननु तर्हि तस्मिन् पुनः सङ्गः स्यात् ? तत्राह---तं देहं स्वाप्न-देहादि-तुल्यं स-प्रपञ्चं पुत्रादि-सहितं पुनर् न भजतेऽहं ममेति नाभिमन्यते । अधिरूढः प्राप्तः समाधि-पर्यन्तो योगो येन । अत एव प्रतिबुद्धं वस्त्व् आत्म-तत्त्वं येन सः ॥३८॥

तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वम् अनुपश्यतः
“what delusion, what grief, for one who sees oneness?”
divine arrangement: the impressions formed previously
तद्-वशेन गच्छन् यावत् स्वारम्भकं कर्मास्ति तावत् प्रतिसमीक्षते जीवत्य् एव
proceeding under its influence, he waits as long as the karma that began this body remains; he lives
“with breath” means with breath and senses
तं देहं स्वाप्न-देहादि-तुल्यं स-प्रपञ्चं पुत्रादि-सहितं पुनर् न भजते
he no longer identifies with that body, with children and the rest, as with a dream-body
he does not regard it as “I” or “mine”
one who has attained yoga culminating in samādhi
अत एव प्रतिबुद्धं वस्त्व् आत्म-तत्त्वं येन सः
therefore he has awakened to the reality of the Self
entries.literal_english: “Thus he is one who has awakened to reality” explains the earlier phrase. Therefore, he experiences only the remaining prārabdha karma, without attachment. As the Īśopaniṣad says: “What delusion, what grief can there be for one who sees oneness?” One may ask how the body continues, ceases, or lives. The answer is that it proceeds according to divine arrangement—the impressions formed previously—and he waits until the karma that began it is exhausted. “With breath” means endowed with breath and senses. One may ask whether attachment to it returns. He does not again identify with that body, complete with children and other relations, as “I” or “mine”; he regards it as a dream-body. He has attained yoga culminating in samādhi; therefore he has awakened to the truth of the Self.

entries.literal_english: In six verses he explains the manner of awakening. Even a son or other relative, though regarded as oneself because of excessive affection, is mortal; “puruṣa” is the seer of the body and the rest.

entries.sanskrit:
पृथग् अवस्थानाभावेऽपि भेदं सदृष्टान्तम् आह---यथोल्मुकाद् इदानीं ज्वलतः काष्ठात् । स्व-सम्भवात् अग्नेः सम्भूतात् । आत्मत्वेनाग्नेः स्वरूपत्वेनाभिमताद् अपि। अत्यन्ताविवेकिनो हि धूमेऽप्य् अग्न्य्-अभिमानोऽस्ति । उल्मुकात् पूर्व-सिद्धाद् अपि तद्-दाहकः प्रकाशकश् चाग्निः पृथग् एव ॥४०॥

भूतादेर् द्रष्टा तेभ्यः पृथक् तस्माद् अपि जीव-संज्ञिताद् ब्रह्म-संज्ञितः पृथक् । तथा प्रधानाद् अपि तत्-प्रवर्तको भगवान् पृथग् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: distinction despite absence of separate location
identification of even smoke with fire

pṛthag avasthānābhāve’pi bhedaṃ sadṛṣṭāntam āha---yatholmukād idānīṃ jvalataḥ kāṣṭhāt | sva-sambhavāt agneḥ sambhūtāt | ātmatvenāgneḥ svarūpatvenābhimatād api| atyantāvivekino hi dhūme’py agny-abhimāno’sti | ulmukāt pūrva-siddhād api tad-dāhakaḥ prakāśakaś cāgniḥ pṛthag eva ||40||

bhūtāder draṣṭā tebhyaḥ pṛthak tasmād api jīva-saṃjñitād brahma-saṃjñitaḥ pṛthak | tathā pradhānād api tat-pravartako bhagavān pṛthag ity arthaḥ ||41||
entries.literal_english: Though things may not occupy separate places, their distinction is illustrated: fire is distinct from the currently burning piece of wood from which it has arisen, even though the extremely undiscriminating identify fire even with smoke. Fire remains separately the illuminator and burner of the fuel.

entries.sanskrit: स्वां स्वांशस्य जीवस्य बन्ध-हेतुं दैवीं देवस्य विष्णोः शक्तिं पराभाव्य तत्-प्रसादेनैव जित्वा स्वरूपेण ब्रह्मत्वेनावतिष्ठते ॥४४॥
word_for_word: स्वां स्वांशस्य जीवस्य बन्ध-हेतुं दैवीं देवस्य विष्णोः शक्तिम्
the divine power of Viṣṇu, which causes bondage for the individual soul, his own portion
conquering through that power’s grace alone
one remains in one’s own nature as Brahman
entries.literal_english: Having subdued the divine power of Viṣṇu—which causes bondage for the individual soul, a portion of the Lord—through that power’s grace alone, one remains in one’s own nature as Brahman.
